name: User
rationale: Authenticated principals share credential and session-related actions.
plain_english_summary: A person who can sign in to iTrust.
source_excerpt: ordinary authenticated user

name: User__mid
rationale: Login and user identity are based on MID.
plain_english_summary: The user's medical ID or system ID used for sign-in.
source_excerpt: Any user can enter their MID and password to gain role-based entry into iTrust.

name: User__password
rationale: Password is needed to model credential entry and credential secrecy requirements.
plain_english_summary: The user's password credential.
source_excerpt: Any user can enter their MID and password to gain role-based entry into iTrust.
alternatives_considered: Model password as a separate Credential entity; rejected because the slice names password as user-entered credential data.

name: User__securityQuestion
rationale: Security question secrecy is explicitly restricted for HCP access.
plain_english_summary: The user's account security question.
source_excerpt: The HCP must not enter, edit, or view the patient's security question or password.
alternatives_considered: Model security question as a separate Credential entity; rejected because the slice only needs a protected user credential field.

name: HCP
rationale: HCP is an actor that creates and edits patients and can be added to provider lists.
plain_english_summary: A health care provider user.
source_excerpt: Important actors include HCP, LHCP, DLHCP, administrator, patient, personal representative, UAP, emergency responder, public health agent, and ordinary authenticated user.

name: LHCP
rationale: LHCP is a specialized provider actor with creation, designation, hospital assignment, and provider-list requirements.
plain_english_summary: A licensed health care provider user.
source_excerpt: Important actors include HCP, LHCP, DLHCP, administrator, patient, personal representative, UAP, emergency responder, public health agent, and ordinary authenticated user.

name: LHCP__specialty
rationale: Administrators must specify a specialty for a new LHCP and patients may search by specialty.
plain_english_summary: The LHCP's medical specialty.
source_excerpt: The administrator must specify the specialty for a new LHCP.
alternatives_considered: Model specialty as an entity; rejected because the slice treats it as search text rather than a managed object.

name: LHCP__hospitals
rationale: Hospital assignments for LHCPs must be representable.
plain_english_summary: The hospitals assigned to the LHCP.
source_excerpt: The administrator can assign an LHCP to multiple hospitals and choose the hospitals.
alternatives_considered: Use a separate assignment entity; rejected because only membership in multiple hospitals is needed in this slice.

name: Administrator
rationale: Administrator is an actor that creates personnel and configures inactivity period length.
plain_english_summary: An administrative iTrust user.
source_excerpt: Important actors include HCP, LHCP, DLHCP, administrator, patient, personal representative, UAP, emergency responder, public health agent, and ordinary authenticated user.

name: Patient
rationale: Patient is both an actor and the subject of records, logs, providers, and demographics.
plain_english_summary: A patient user in iTrust.
source_excerpt: Important actors include HCP, LHCP, DLHCP, administrator, patient, personal representative, UAP, emergency responder, public health agent, and ordinary authenticated user.

name: Patient__name
rationale: New patient creation initially includes the patient's name.
plain_english_summary: The patient's name.
source_excerpt: Only the patient's name and email are initially provided by the HCP.

name: Patient__email
rationale: New patient creation initially includes the patient's email.
plain_english_summary: The patient's email address.
source_excerpt: Only the patient's name and email are initially provided by the HCP.

name: Patient__mid
rationale: Patient MID is explicitly non-editable, so it must be representable.
plain_english_summary: The patient's medical ID.
source_excerpt: The HCP can edit patient data according to the data format, but the patient's MID must not be editable.
alternatives_considered: Reuse User.mid only; rejected because the requirement specifically refers to the patient's MID on patient data.

name: Patient__designatedProviders
rationale: Patient-specific DLHCP designation is modeled as a relationship rather than a separate principal type.
plain_english_summary: The LHCPs designated by this patient as designated providers.
source_excerpt: A patient can designate any LHCP as a DLHCP for that patient and can undesignate any LHCP as a DLHCP for that patient.
alternatives_considered: Model DLHCP as a separate principal type; rejected because the spec says designation is for that patient.

name: Patient__providerList
rationale: Provider-list additions need a patient-owned list of providers.
plain_english_summary: The providers on the patient's provider list.
source_excerpt: A patient can add a LHCP/HCP to their provider list by searching by name, specialty, and optionally zip code.
alternatives_considered: Model provider list as only a separate resource; rejected because direct patient-to-provider membership supports simple authorization checks.

name: Patient__visitedProviders
rationale: Patients can view LHCPs they have ever had office visits with.
plain_english_summary: The LHCPs who have had office visits with the patient.
source_excerpt: A patient can view all LHCPs the patient has ever had an office visit with and all LHCPs the patient has designated.
alternatives_considered: Derive only from OfficeVisit records; rejected because the slice directly requires a viewable list.

name: Patient__personalRepresentatives
rationale: Represented-patient access requires knowing which users represent the patient.
plain_english_summary: The users who are personal representatives for this patient.
source_excerpt: for records of patients for whom the user is a personal representative
alternatives_considered: Store represented patients on PersonalRepresentative; either direction works, but this keeps ownership on the patient whose records are accessed.

name: PersonalRepresentative
rationale: Personal representatives have explicit medical-record viewing permissions.
plain_english_summary: A user who can act on behalf of a patient for record access.
source_excerpt: Important actors include HCP, LHCP, DLHCP, administrator, patient, personal representative, UAP, emergency responder, public health agent, and ordinary authenticated user.

name: UAP
rationale: UAP users are created by LHCPs.
plain_english_summary: A user with UAP role in iTrust.
source_excerpt: Important actors include HCP, LHCP, DLHCP, administrator, patient, personal representative, UAP, emergency responder, public health agent, and ordinary authenticated user.

name: EmergencyResponder
rationale: Emergency responders are personnel created by administrators.
plain_english_summary: An emergency responder user.
source_excerpt: Important actors include HCP, LHCP, DLHCP, administrator, patient, personal representative, UAP, emergency responder, public health agent, and ordinary authenticated user.

name: PublicHealthAgent
rationale: Public health agents are personnel created by administrators.
plain_english_summary: A public health agent user.
source_excerpt: Important actors include HCP, LHCP, DLHCP, administrator, patient, personal representative, UAP, emergency responder, public health agent, and ordinary authenticated user.

name: Hospital
rationale: Hospitals are assigned to LHCPs by administrators.
plain_english_summary: A hospital that an LHCP may be assigned to.
source_excerpt: The administrator can assign an LHCP to multiple hospitals and choose the hospitals.

name: MedicalRecord
rationale: Medical records are patient-owned resources viewed by patients and representatives.
plain_english_summary: A patient's medical record.
source_excerpt: Important resources include patients, personnel, medical records, demographic information, provider designations, access logs, sessions, credentials, and provider lists.

name: MedicalRecord__patient
rationale: Own-record and represented-record checks require the record's patient.
plain_english_summary: The patient whose medical record this is.
source_excerpt: for their own records and for records of patients for whom the user is a personal representative
alternatives_considered: Use context.patient on every record-view action; rejected because ownership is persistent record data.

name: MedicalRecord__includesFamilyHistory
rationale: The slice explicitly includes family history within medical records.
plain_english_summary: Whether this medical record includes family history information.
source_excerpt: A patient or personal representative may view medical records including family history.
alternatives_considered: Model FamilyHistory as a separate resource; rejected because the requirement treats it as included in medical records.

name: MedicalRecord__hasPersonalHealthInformation
rationale: Personal health information is a named category visible in own or represented records.
plain_english_summary: Whether this record contains personal health information.
source_excerpt: The patient or personal representative can see patient personal health information, immunizations, and office visit information for their own records and the records for whom the user is a personal representative.
alternatives_considered: Model PersonalHealthInformation as a separate resource; rejected because the slice only requires visibility of record contents.

name: MedicalRecord__hasImmunizations
rationale: Immunizations are a named category visible in own or represented records.
plain_english_summary: Whether this record contains immunization information.
source_excerpt: The patient or personal representative can see patient personal health information, immunizations, and office visit information for their own records and the records for whom the user is a personal representative.
alternatives_considered: Model Immunization as a separate resource; rejected because the slice only requires visibility of record contents.

name: MedicalRecord__hasOfficeVisitInformation
rationale: Office-visit information is a named category visible in own or represented records.
plain_english_summary: Whether this record contains office-visit information.
source_excerpt: The patient or personal representative can see patient personal health information, immunizations, and office visit information for their own records and the records for whom the user is a personal representative.
alternatives_considered: Model OfficeVisitInformation as a separate resource; rejected because the slice only requires visibility of record contents.

name: AccessLog
rationale: Patients can view their own access logs over a selected period.
plain_english_summary: A log of accesses to a patient's information.
source_excerpt: Important resources include patients, personnel, medical records, demographic information, provider designations, access logs, sessions, credentials, and provider lists.

name: AccessLog__patient
rationale: Own-access-log checks require the log's patient owner.
plain_english_summary: The patient whose access log this is.
source_excerpt: A patient can view the patient's own access log.

name: AccessLog__accessorName
rationale: Access-log results contain the accessor name.
plain_english_summary: The name of the person who accessed the patient's information.
source_excerpt: The access-log result contains the accessor name, the accessor role relative to the patient, the access timestamp, and the transaction type.
alternatives_considered: Use accessor User entity; rejected because the result field is stated as a name.

name: AccessLog__accessorRole
rationale: Access-log results contain the accessor role relative to the patient.
plain_english_summary: The accessor's relationship or role relative to the patient.
source_excerpt: The access-log result contains the accessor name, the accessor role relative to the patient, the access timestamp, and the transaction type.
alternatives_considered: Use a Role enum; rejected because relative-to-patient roles may be relationship descriptions.

name: AccessLog__accessTimestamp
rationale: Access-log results and date-range filtering need timestamps.
plain_english_summary: When the access happened.
source_excerpt: The access-log result contains the accessor name, the accessor role relative to the patient, the access timestamp, and the transaction type.

name: AccessLog__transactionType
rationale: Access-log results contain the transaction type.
plain_english_summary: The kind of access transaction recorded in the log.
source_excerpt: The access-log result contains the accessor name, the accessor role relative to the patient, the access timestamp, and the transaction type.
alternatives_considered: Use a TransactionType enum; rejected because the slice does not enumerate possible transaction types.

name: Session
rationale: Resource-less login, logout, and authorization-disable checks need a schema resource and session state.
plain_english_summary: An authenticated iTrust session.
source_excerpt: Important resources include patients, personnel, medical records, demographic information, provider designations, access logs, sessions, credentials, and provider lists.

name: Session__user
rationale: Session actions and inactivity are tied to the logged-in user.
plain_english_summary: The user who owns the session.
source_excerpt: An authenticated session ends when the user logs out or closes the application.

name: Session__isAuthenticated
rationale: Authorization must be disabled after inactivity limit is exceeded, so authenticated state must be representable.
plain_english_summary: Whether the session is currently authenticated and authorized.
source_excerpt: after the inactivity limit is exceeded, all authorization is disabled.

name: Session__lastActivityAt
rationale: Inactivity termination depends on time since last activity.
plain_english_summary: The time of the last activity in the session.
source_excerpt: Electronic sessions must terminate after the configured inactivity period; after the inactivity limit is exceeded, all authorization is disabled.

name: SystemConfiguration
rationale: The administrator sets the global inactivity period length.
plain_english_summary: System-wide iTrust configuration settings.
source_excerpt: The administrator can set the inactivity period length.

name: SystemConfiguration__inactivityPeriodLength
rationale: The configured inactivity period length is explicitly administrator-controlled.
plain_english_summary: How long a session may be inactive before authorization is disabled.
source_excerpt: The administrator can set the inactivity period length.

name: ProviderSearch
rationale: Provider-list additions are performed by searching on name, specialty, and optional zip code.
plain_english_summary: A provider search request used to find providers to add.
source_excerpt: A patient can add a LHCP/HCP to their provider list by searching by name, specialty, and optionally zip code.

name: ProviderSearch__name
rationale: Provider search may use provider name.
plain_english_summary: The provider name entered in the search.
source_excerpt: searching by name, specialty, and optionally zip code

name: ProviderSearch__specialty
rationale: Provider search may use provider specialty.
plain_english_summary: The specialty entered in the provider search.
source_excerpt: searching by name, specialty, and optionally zip code

name: ProviderSearch__zipCode
rationale: Zip code is explicitly optional in provider search.
plain_english_summary: The optional zip code entered in the provider search.
source_excerpt: searching by name, specialty, and optionally zip code

name: createPatient
rationale: HCPs can create patient users.
plain_english_summary: Create a new patient in iTrust.
source_excerpt: An HCP can create a patient and enter the patient as a new user of the system.

name: editPatientData
rationale: HCPs can edit patient data except protected fields handled by policy.
plain_english_summary: Edit patient demographic or profile data.
source_excerpt: The HCP can edit patient data according to the data format, but the patient's MID must not be editable.

name: viewPatientCredential
rationale: Credential viewing is explicitly mentioned as prohibited for HCPs and needs an action for Stage 2.
plain_english_summary: View a patient's security question or password.
source_excerpt: The HCP must not enter, edit, or view the patient's security question or password.

credentialField.name: viewPatientCredential__context__credentialField
credentialField.rationale: The policy needs to distinguish password and security question credential fields.
credentialField.plain_english_summary: Which credential field is being viewed.
credentialField.source_excerpt: The HCP must not enter, edit, or view the patient's security question or password.

name: editPatientCredential
rationale: Credential editing is explicitly mentioned as prohibited for HCPs and needs an action for Stage 2.
plain_english_summary: Edit a patient's security question or password.
source_excerpt: The HCP must not enter, edit, or view the patient's security question or password.

credentialField.name: editPatientCredential__context__credentialField
credentialField.rationale: The policy needs to distinguish password and security question credential fields.
credentialField.plain_english_summary: Which credential field is being edited.
credentialField.source_excerpt: The HCP must not enter, edit, or view the patient's security question or password.

name: createLHCP
rationale: Administrators can create LHCPs.
plain_english_summary: Create a new LHCP user.
source_excerpt: An administrator can create LHCPs, emergency responders, and public health agents.

name: createEmergencyResponder
rationale: Administrators can create emergency responders.
plain_english_summary: Create a new emergency responder user.
source_excerpt: An administrator can create LHCPs, emergency responders, and public health agents.

name: createPublicHealthAgent
rationale: Administrators can create public health agents.
plain_english_summary: Create a new public health agent user.
source_excerpt: An administrator can create LHCPs, emergency responders, and public health agents.

name: assignLHCPToHospitals
rationale: Administrators assign LHCPs to multiple chosen hospitals.
plain_english_summary: Assign an LHCP to one or more hospitals.
source_excerpt: The administrator can assign an LHCP to multiple hospitals and choose the hospitals.

hospitals.name: assignLHCPToHospitals__context__hospitals
hospitals.rationale: The assignment operation must carry the selected hospitals.
hospitals.plain_english_summary: The hospitals selected for the LHCP.
hospitals.source_excerpt: The administrator can assign an LHCP to multiple hospitals and choose the hospitals.

name: createUAP
rationale: LHCPs can create UAP users.
plain_english_summary: Create a new UAP user.
source_excerpt: A LHCP can create UAP users.

name: login
rationale: Any user can enter credentials to gain role-based entry.
plain_english_summary: Sign in to iTrust using MID and password.
source_excerpt: Any user can enter their MID and password to gain role-based entry into iTrust.

mid.name: login__context__mid
mid.rationale: Login requires the MID entered by the user.
mid.source_excerpt: Any user can enter their MID and password to gain role-based entry into iTrust.

password.name: login__context__password
password.rationale: Login requires the password entered by the user.
password.source_excerpt: Any user can enter their MID and password to gain role-based entry into iTrust.

name: requestPasswordChange
rationale: Any user can request a password change.
plain_english_summary: Ask to change the user's password.
source_excerpt: Any user can request a password change.

name: logout
rationale: Authenticated sessions end when users log out.
plain_english_summary: Log out of an iTrust session.
source_excerpt: An authenticated session ends when the user logs out or closes the application.

name: closeApplication
rationale: Authenticated sessions end when users close the application.
plain_english_summary: Close the iTrust application session.
source_excerpt: An authenticated session ends when the user logs out or closes the application.

name: setInactivityPeriodLength
rationale: Administrators configure the inactivity period length.
plain_english_summary: Set how long sessions may be inactive.
source_excerpt: The administrator can set the inactivity period length.

newLength.name: setInactivityPeriodLength__context__newLength
newLength.rationale: The set operation must carry the requested inactivity period length.
newLength.source_excerpt: The administrator can set the inactivity period length.

name: viewPastAndDesignatedLHCPs
rationale: Patients can view LHCPs from visits and designations.
plain_english_summary: View the patient's past and designated LHCPs.
source_excerpt: A patient can view all LHCPs the patient has ever had an office visit with and all LHCPs the patient has designated.

name: searchProviders
rationale: Adding to a provider list begins with a provider search.
plain_english_summary: Search for providers by name, specialty, and optional zip code.
source_excerpt: A patient can add a LHCP/HCP to their provider list by searching by name, specialty, and optionally zip code.

name: addProviderToList
rationale: Patients can add HCP or LHCP providers to their provider list.
plain_english_summary: Add a provider to the patient's provider list.
source_excerpt: A patient can add a LHCP/HCP to their provider list by searching by name, specialty, and optionally zip code.

provider.name: addProviderToList__context__provider
provider.rationale: The operation must identify the provider being added.
provider.plain_english_summary: The provider to add to the patient's list.
provider.source_excerpt: A patient can add a LHCP/HCP to their provider list by searching by name, specialty, and optionally zip code.

name: designateDLHCP
rationale: Patients can designate any LHCP as a DLHCP for that patient.
plain_english_summary: Mark an LHCP as the patient's designated provider.
source_excerpt: A patient can designate any LHCP as a DLHCP for that patient and can undesignate any LHCP as a DLHCP for that patient.

lhcp.name: designateDLHCP__context__lhcp
lhcp.rationale: The designation operation must identify the LHCP being designated.
lhcp.source_excerpt: A patient can designate any LHCP as a DLHCP for that patient and can undesignate any LHCP as a DLHCP for that patient.

name: undesignateDLHCP
rationale: Patients can remove a DLHCP designation for that patient.
plain_english_summary: Remove an LHCP from the patient's designated-provider list.
source_excerpt: A patient can designate any LHCP as a DLHCP for that patient and can undesignate any LHCP as a DLHCP for that patient.

lhcp.name: undesignateDLHCP__context__lhcp
lhcp.rationale: The undesignation operation must identify the LHCP being undesignated.
lhcp.source_excerpt: A patient can designate any LHCP as a DLHCP for that patient and can undesignate any LHCP as a DLHCP for that patient.

name: viewAccessLog
rationale: Patients can view their own access log and choose a date period.
plain_english_summary: View a patient's access log for a selected date range.
source_excerpt: A patient can view the patient's own access log. The patient can choose a beginning and end date for the access-log period.

beginDate.name: viewAccessLog__context__beginDate
beginDate.rationale: The access-log period has a chosen beginning date.
beginDate.plain_english_summary: The start of the access-log date range.
beginDate.source_excerpt: A patient can view the patient's own access log. The patient can choose a beginning and end date for the access-log period.

endDate.name: viewAccessLog__context__endDate
endDate.rationale: The access-log period has a chosen end date.
endDate.plain_english_summary: The end of the access-log date range.
endDate.source_excerpt: A patient can view the patient's own access log. The patient can choose a beginning and end date for the access-log period.

name: viewMedicalRecord
rationale: Patients and personal representatives may view medical records including family history.
plain_english_summary: View a patient's medical record.
source_excerpt: A patient or personal representative may view medical records including family history.

name: seeRecordHealthInformation
rationale: Patients and personal representatives can see named health information categories in own or represented records.
plain_english_summary: See personal health, immunization, and office-visit information in a medical record.
source_excerpt: A patient or personal representative can see patient personal health information, immunizations, and office-visit information for their own records and for records of patients for whom the user is a personal representative.

informationCategory.name: seeRecordHealthInformation__context__informationCategory
informationCategory.rationale: The action covers the named categories personal health information, immunizations, and office-visit information.
informationCategory.plain_english_summary: Which type of record information is being viewed.
informationCategory.source_excerpt: A patient or personal representative can see patient personal health information, immunizations, and office-visit information for their own records and for records of patients for whom the user is a personal representative.
